Ceiling and floor of the same explicit sequence are thus governed by different mathematics: the
ceiling by nothing (Theorem 4), the floor by the parity of the integer relations among the
ordinates (Theorem 6). Under RH the infimum is never attained at an `n ≥ 2`; whether it equals
`−a_1` is a Diophantine statement, and `inf a_n < 0` in every case (Theorem 5).

## 7. A discrete criterion left open

For a fixed base `b ≥ 2`, is RH equivalent to boundedness above of the single subsequence
`(a_{b^m})_{m≥1}`? The direction ⟹ is Theorem 3. For ⟸ the generating function
`Σ_m a_{b^m}z^m = Σ_ρ w_ρ/(1 − b^{ρ−½}z)` has poles at `b^{½−ρ}`; bounded coefficients force
analyticity in `|z| < 1`, contradicting an off-line pole unless that pole is an accumulation point
of other poles — a sequence of zeros with real parts converging to the supremal abscissa and
`b^{iγ_j} → 1`. The Landau route meets the same configuration. The continuous criterion (Theorem 2)
avoids it because `ξ` has no real zeros. Excluding this `b`-resonance is the open core.

## 8. Numerical illustration (no proof depends on it)

For `n ≤ 2·10^7`: `max a_n = 0.018674` at `n = 3100` (`0.40·a_1`), `min a_n = −0.022681` at
`n = 319439`, no `n` with `a_n > a_1`, record sites `6, 15, 34, 205–208, 3084–3100`; the powers of
two oscillate in sign with `|a_{2^m}| ≤ 0.0173`.

## 9. Relation to the literature

Classical criteria of this type are two-sided and lose a power of a logarithm: RH ⟺
`|ψ(x) − x| ≤ √x log²x/(8π)` for `x ≥ 73.2` (Schoenfeld 1976), or `ψ(x) = x + O(√x log²x)`. The
integer criteria of Robin (1984), Lagarias (2002) and Nicolas concern `σ(n)` and `φ(n)` with the
constant `e^γ`. The kernel `1/(ρ(1−ρ))` makes the zero side absolutely convergent, which is why the
present criterion needs no logarithm, is one-sided (Landau), and has an exact constant equal to
its own value at `n = 1`. The recurrence and floor arguments are Bohr's almost periodicity and
Kronecker's theorem, in the tradition of Ingham's Ω-results and of the linear-independence
hypothesis used by Montgomery and by Rubinstein–Sarnak; the parity characterisation of the floor
appears to be new, as does the unconditional `Ω±` law with the exact positive constant.

## Addendum: the unconditional frontier (Lean, `WeilLagFunctionFrontier`)

`|Φ(L)| ≤ C e^{L/2} e^{−c L^{1/10}}` and `|a_n| ≤ C √n e^{−c (log n)^{1/10}}` for large `L`, `n`, from the corpus PNT with
error term via `M(x) − log x + γ = E(x)/x − ∫_x^∞ E(t)t^{−2}dt`. RH is exponent `0`; provable is exponent `½`; every
exponent in between is a fixed-width zero-free region. See STATUS MUST-242.

## Addendum: the Gram interface (Lean, `WeilLagFunctionGram`)

RH ⟺ `K(x,y) = Φ(log x − log y)` positive semidefinite on `(ℝ_{>0}, ×)` ⟺ all `(Φ(log(n/m)))_{n,m≤N}` PSD. Under RH the form
is `Σ_ρ w_ρ |Σ c_x x^{iγ}|²`; the converse uses the `2×2` minors on `{1,n}` = `2(a_1 − a_n)`. This is the interface a
geometric producer must fill (STATUS MUST-243).

## Addendum: the carrier form (Lean, `WeilLagFunctionCarrier`)

On functions of the zero copies, `B(f,g) = Σ_ρ f(ρ)g(1−ρ)/(ρ(1−ρ))` and `v_x(ρ) = x^{ρ−½}` give `B(v_x,v_y) = Φ(log x − log y)`
unconditionally; RH ⟺ `B ≥ 0` on the Frobenius orbit. This is the Hodge datum in carrier language (STATUS MUST-243).

## Addendum: dense lag sets (Lean, `WeilLagFunctionDense`)

Continuity of `Φ` + density: RH ⟺ `Φ` bounded above on `{k log p + l log q}` for any two distinct primes (`{p,q}`-rationals).

# Quadratic divisor-front factor

- **ID:** quadratic-divisor-front-factor
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean)
- **Source:** `ca_bulk_edge_manuscript_revised.pdf`, §9, equation (52)
- **Statement:** In `ℚ⟦X⟧`, the exact quadratic local correction `q = X²(1-X)/(1-X²)` satisfies `(1-X²)(1+q)=1-X³` and has coefficients `q₂=1`, `q₃=-1`, `q₄=1`.

## Goal

Give future divisor-front work a denominator-free, hypothesis-free formal-series interface for the
first nontrivial local layer. This deliberately formalizes only the exact algebraic input to the
paper's asymptotic expansion, not its RH-conditional or analytic claims.

## Gates

- [x] 0 → 1 in-progress: source-pure exact residue, routine proof, no RH or numerical input
- [x] 1 → 2 fully-proven: complete proof below; dependencies are formal power-series geometric
  inversion and coefficient convolution
- [x] 2 → 3 formalized: Lean theorem `quadraticLayerCorrection_initial_jet` in
  `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/QuadraticDivisorFrontFactor.lean`; source check and targeted
  build green; axiom audit is only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`
- [ ] 3 → 4 publication-ready: not a publication claim; `[REDISCOVERED]` algebraic bridge

## Paper proof

Let `G = 1 + X² + X⁴ + ⋯`; formally, `(1-X²)G=1`. Define
`q = X²(1-X)G`. Then

`(1-X²)(1+q) = 1-X² + X²(1-X)((1-X²)G) = 1-X³`.

The first coefficients of `G` are `G₀=1`, `G₁=0`, `G₂=1`; convolution gives
`q₂=G₀=1`, `q₃=-G₀+G₁=-1`, and `q₄=G₂-G₁=1`. This is exact in `ℚ⟦X⟧` and has no hypotheses.

## Audit

- **Internal:** no existing superior/colossally-abundant or Lambert-`W` layer interface. The
  available Lambert series are different transforms.
- **External:** `[REDISCOVERED]`; finite geometric-series algebra, not new scientific knowledge.
- **Open core for full §9:** coefficient control for `log(1+q)` after formal substitution, then
  analytic realization. This card does not claim either step.

## Log

- 2026-08-17 — created in 1-in-progress; exact residue isolated from the manuscript.
- 2026-08-17 — formalized as `quadraticLayerEvenGeom_mul_denominator`,
  `quadraticLayerFrontFactor`, and `quadraticLayerCorrection_initial_jet`; wired into RHTower.

Finite packets, jets, homology, local indices, multiplicities, and real-zero determinants can be realized without fixing horizontal position. Nested-aperture subtraction localizes the live Ramaré front to activation-seam polarization, seam norm, incidence-energy variation, and source-scale response-defect fourth moment. Fixed-arity local Hall transport and source-disjoint `l1` centering are impossible. FZZ defeats every finite normalized density constant and even positive singular Hilbert reflection is nonselective. S6F/TCD show identical finite positive data realize either crossing sign. LI and HB likewise show that real derivative towers or finite-energy two-leg Hilbert realizations do not determine global phase/orientation. Successful selectors require infinite coefficient provenance plus source-uniform complex order and source-semantic interface constraints.

Target cardinality is also closed at fixed occupied dimension. One determinant-optimal positive covariance controls capture of an arbitrary bounded, even uncountable, target family with cost equal to occupied dimension times one worst-target quadratic moment; the same law excludes post-ramp re-entry and has a quenched probability form. Thus continuum union bounds and target enumeration are not route cores. U's remaining issue is stronger: the present one-target scalar moment/action package permits exact sparse quadratic escape with summable entries, so only a literal-source cross-degree or history-coupled law can change its frontier.

### 3. Orientation is the common missing datum

Scalar positivity, absolute values, determinants, unitary gauges, positive diagonal completion, and common modular gain repeatedly erase the sign distinguishing a zero from its reflection. Ordinary probability and equal total mass coexist with negative reflected squares and maximal total-variation separation. Regular Hardy Gram geometry is blind to the inner factor. No positive operator can carry the signed centered-Xi divisor through a zero-free-gauge spectral determinant. APF supplies rigid negative winding but completion cannot nucleate charge; HB supplies copywise beat and helicity classifiers; FD2 supplies correct signed Xi occurrence, but positive polarization changes it and exact indefinite polarization cannot orient it. C1 now has an exact reflection-twisted Weil target, but no coefficient-faithful class-space source realization of that target. P separates two facts: its canonical Hellinger determinant has the wrong divisor, while its faithful arithmetic circulant cubic has the correct rectangle multiplicity but counts every enclosed zero without horizontal selection. CTF supplies a second source-defined exact occurrence: its geometric Euler/Hilbert trace defect has exactly the zeta divisor on the open strip, but no reflection or orientation law. P's modular triple retains abstract orientation, yet the fixed literal reference has zero value under every total compatible sigma-trace and every finite prime-depth scalar reweighting. A source-derived strict-right zero-charge law, nonadmitted boundary/trace defect, moving-reference current, or CTF fusion-reflection sign is therefore required; generic winding, exact Mellin occurrence, or twisted-trace existence is insufficient. For most complexes, remaining problem is coefficient-faithful source orientation of correct occurrence. RG is the important exception: occurrence and orientation are encoded already, and remaining problem is uniform arithmetic order of the literal atomic--continuous discrepancy on a cofinal heat family.

## Cross-route conclusions

### 1. Source/receiver firewall

Most routes possess a sharp RH-equivalent receiver. Rewriting it as positivity, passivity, flatness, determinant convergence, bounded energy, KMS exchange, or spectral completeness does not advance RH unless Lean derives the premise from literal source before choosing a zero. RG crosses more of this firewall than most labels. CCM-FU/CFI/SP-E cross it jointly: completed Abel and RG weighted mass-error are one scale connection whose floor mixture reduces to one signed triangular transform after bounded affine/reset channels. Weighted first-moment growth, central unit-Riesz barycenter, every regular causal-depth trace assembly, and unframed chiral spectralization are terminal. D2 boundary propagation is RH-equivalent and fails on a boundary-blind not-RH window. LI's real shape tests admit a negative fourth mode. E's bounded-density histories, fixed common-spectator arity, source-disjoint `l1` centering, stable seam inversion, and complete-prime/polynomial-prefix identification and diagonal Gamma--Hankel Möbius reconstruction cannot supply integer-prefix cancellation. HB's angular occurrence is closed at the first live order-`2m` jet and its unique entire normalization, including fixed simple inverse boundary poles; the original doubled Xi divisor is retained, and its operator/passive/clock/finite-energy radial mechanisms remain nonselective. FZZ-P has off-wall external-BRST occurrence yet no integrated mixed Ward orientation law. L has source cyclicity and a complete Burnol receiver, but every fixed reader that kills vertical ambiguity already forces trivial source holonomy. module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.GeomSum
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Divisors
public import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
public import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum.Prime
public import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

/-!
# Factorisation properties of natural numbers

This file defines abundant, pseudoperfect, deficient, and weird numbers and formalizes their
relations with prime and perfect numbers.

## Main Definitions

* `Nat.Abundant`: a natural number `n` is _abundant_ if the sum of its proper divisors is greater
  than `n`
* `Nat.Pseudoperfect`: a natural number `n` is _pseudoperfect_ if the sum of a subset of its proper
  divisors equals `n`
* `Nat.Deficient`: a natural number `n` is _deficient_ if the sum of its proper divisors is less
  than `n`
* `Nat.Weird`: a natural number is _weird_ if it is abundant but not pseudoperfect

## Main Results

* `Nat.deficient_or_perfect_or_abundant`: A positive natural number is either deficient,
  perfect, or abundant.
* `Nat.Prime.deficient`: All prime natural numbers are deficient.
* `Nat.infinite_deficient`: There are infinitely many deficient numbers.
* `Nat.Prime.deficient_pow`: Any natural number power of a prime is deficient.

## Implementation Notes
* Zero is not included in any of the definitions and these definitions only apply to natural
  numbers greater than zero.

## References
* [R. W. Prielipp, *PERFECT NUMBERS, ABUNDANT NUMBERS, AND DEFICIENT NUMBERS*][Prielipp1970]

## Tags

abundant, deficient, weird, pseudoperfect
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset

namespace Nat

variable {n m p : ℕ}

/-- `n : ℕ` is _abundant_ if the sum of the proper divisors of `n` is greater than `n`. -/
def Abundant (n : ℕ) : Prop := n < ∑ i ∈ properDivisors n, i
deriving Decidable

/-- `n : ℕ` is _deficient_ if the sum of the proper divisors of `n` is less than `n`. -/
def Deficient (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∑ i ∈ properDivisors n, i < n
deriving Decidable

/-- A positive natural number `n` is _pseudoperfect_ if there exists a subset of the proper
  divisors of `n` such that the sum of that subset is equal to `n`. -/
def Pseudoperfect (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < n ∧ ∃ s ⊆ properDivisors n, ∑ i ∈ s, i = n
deriving Decidable

/-- `n : ℕ` is a _weird_ number if and only if it is abundant but not pseudoperfect. -/
def Weird (n : ℕ) : Prop := Abundant n ∧ ¬ Pseudoperfect n
deriving Decidable

/-- `abundancyIndex n` is the sum of the divisors of `n` divided by `n`. -/
def abundancyIndex (n : ℕ) : ℚ := (∑ i ∈ n.divisors, i) / (n : ℚ)

theorem not_pseudoperfect_iff_forall :
    ¬ Pseudoperfect n ↔ n = 0 ∨ ∀ s ⊆ properDivisors n, ∑ i ∈ s, i ≠ n := by
  grind [Pseudoperfect]

theorem not_deficient_zero : ¬ Deficient 0 := by
  decide

theorem deficient_one : Deficient 1 := by
  decide

theorem deficient_two : Deficient 2 := by
  decide

theorem deficient_three : Deficient 3 := by
  decide

theorem not_abundant_zero : ¬ Abundant 0 := by
  decide

theorem abundant_twelve : Abundant 12 := by
  decide

theorem not_weird_zero : ¬ Weird 0 := by
  decide

theorem weird_seventy : Weird 70 := by
  decide +kernel

lemma Deficient.pos (h : Deficient n) : 0 < n := by
  grind only [not_deficient_zero]

lemma Abundant.pos (h : Abundant n) : 0 < n := by
  grind only [not_abundant_zero]

lemma Weird.pos (h : Weird n) : 0 < n := by
  grind only [not_weird_zero]

lemma deficient_iff_not_abundant_and_not_perfect (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    Deficient n ↔ ¬ Abundant n ∧ ¬ Perfect n := by
  grind [Perfect, Abundant, Deficient]

lemma perfect_iff_not_abundant_and_not_deficient (hn : 0 ≠ n) :
    Perfect n ↔ ¬ Abundant n ∧ ¬ Deficient n := by
  grind [Perfect, Abundant, Deficient]

lemma abundant_iff_not_perfect_and_not_deficient (hn : 0 ≠ n) :
    Abundant n ↔ ¬ Perfect n ∧ ¬ Deficient n := by
  grind [Perfect, Abundant, Deficient]

/-- A positive natural number is either deficient, perfect, or abundant -/
theorem deficient_or_perfect_or_abundant (hn : 0 ≠ n) :
    Deficient n ∨ Abundant n ∨ Perfect n := by
  grind [Perfect, Abundant, Deficient]

theorem Perfect.pseudoperfect (h : Perfect n) : Pseudoperfect n :=
  ⟨h.2, ⟨properDivisors n, ⟨fun _ a ↦ a, h.1⟩⟩⟩

theorem Prime.not_abundant (h : Prime n) : ¬ Abundant n :=
  fun h1 ↦ (h.one_lt.trans h1).ne' (sum_properDivisors_eq_one_iff_prime.mpr h)

theorem Prime.not_weird (h : Prime n) : ¬ Weird n := by
  grind [Weird, h.not_abundant]

theorem Prime.not_pseudoperfect (h : Prime p) : ¬ Pseudoperfect p := by
  rw [not_pseudoperfect_iff_forall]
  refine Or.inr fun s hs ↦ ne_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt ?_ h.one_lt)
  rw [Prime.properDivisors h] at hs
  simpa using Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset hs

theorem Prime.not_perfect (h : Prime p) : ¬ Perfect p :=
  fun hp ↦ h.not_pseudoperfect hp.pseudoperfect

/-- Any natural number power of a prime is deficient -/

Or.inr fun s hs ↦ ne_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt ?_ h.one_lt)
  rw [Prime.properDivisors h] at hs
  simpa using Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset hs

theorem Prime.not_perfect (h : Prime p) : ¬ Perfect p :=
  fun hp ↦ h.not_pseudoperfect hp.pseudoperfect

/-- Any natural number power of a prime is deficient -/
theorem Prime.deficient_pow (h : Prime n) : Deficient (n ^ m) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with (rfl | _)
  · simpa using deficient_one
  · rw [Deficient, properDivisors_prime_pow h]
    calc
      ∑ x ∈ Finset.map ⟨(n ^ ·), Nat.pow_right_injective h.two_le⟩ (range m), x
        = ∑ i ∈ range m, n ^ i := by simp
      _ = (n ^ m - 1) / (n - 1) := (Nat.geomSum_eq (Prime.two_le h) _)
      _ ≤ (n ^ m - 1) := Nat.div_le_self (n ^ m - 1) (n - 1)
      _ < n ^ m := sub_lt (pow_pos (Prime.pos h) m) (Nat.one_pos)

theorem _root_.IsPrimePow.deficient (h : IsPrimePow n) : Deficient n := by
  obtain ⟨p, k, hp, -, rfl⟩ := h
  exact hp.nat_prime.deficient_pow

theorem Prime.deficient (h : Prime n) : Deficient n :=
  (pow_one n) ▸ h.deficient_pow

/-- There exists infinitely many deficient numbers -/
theorem infinite_deficient : {n : ℕ | n.Deficient}.Infinite := by
  rw [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  intro a
  obtain ⟨b, h1, h2⟩ := exists_infinite_primes a.succ
  exact ⟨b, h2.deficient, h1⟩

theorem infinite_even_deficient : {n : ℕ | Even n ∧ n.Deficient}.Infinite := by
  rw [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  intro n
  use 2 ^ (n + 1)
  constructor
  · exact ⟨⟨2 ^ n, by rw [pow_succ, mul_two]⟩, prime_two.deficient_pow⟩
  · calc
      n ≤ 2 ^ n := Nat.le_of_lt n.lt_two_pow_self
      _ < 2 ^ (n + 1) := (Nat.pow_lt_pow_iff_right (Nat.one_lt_two)).mpr (lt_add_one n)

theorem infinite_odd_deficient : {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ n.Deficient}.Infinite := by
  rw [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  intro n
  obtain ⟨p, ⟨_, h2⟩⟩ := exists_infinite_primes (max (n + 1) 3)
  exact ⟨p, Set.mem_setOf.mpr ⟨Prime.odd_of_ne_two h2 (Ne.symm (ne_of_lt (by grind))),
    Prime.deficient h2⟩, by grind⟩

theorem abundant_iff_sum_divisors : Abundant n ↔ 2 * n < ∑ i ∈ n.divisors, i := by
  grind [Abundant, sum_divisors_eq_sum_properDivisors_add_self]

theorem abundant_iff_two_lt_abundancyIndex : Abundant n ↔ 2 < n.abundancyIndex := by
  by_cases h : n = 0
  · simp [h, Abundant, abundancyIndex]
  · rw [abundant_iff_sum_divisors, abundancyIndex, lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
    norm_cast

theorem abundancyIndex_le_of_dvd (hn : n ≠ 0) (hd : m ∣ n) :
    m.abundancyIndex ≤ n.abundancyIndex := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hd
  have hk0 : k ≠ 0 := by grind
  rw [abundancyIndex, abundancyIndex, hk, cast_mul, div_mul_eq_div_div_swap]
  refine div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ?_ m.cast_nonneg
  rw [le_div_iff₀ (by grind [cast_pos]), ← cast_mul, cast_le, sum_mul]
  exact (sum_image (f := fun i ↦ i) (mul_left_injective₀ hk0).injOn).symm.trans_le
    (sum_le_sum_of_subset (by grind [mul_dvd_mul_iff_right hk0]))

theorem Abundant.of_dvd (h : Abundant m) (hd : m ∣ n) (hn : n ≠ 0) : Abundant n := by
  have := abundancyIndex_le_of_dvd hn hd
  grind [abundant_iff_two_lt_abundancyIndex]

theorem Abundant.mul_left (h : Abundant n) (hm : m ≠ 0) : Abundant (m * n) := by
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := by grind [not_abundant_zero]
  have hmn : m * n ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero hm hn
  exact Abundant.of_dvd h (Nat.dvd_mul_left n m) hmn

theorem infinite_even_abundant : {n : ℕ | Even n ∧ n.Abundant}.Infinite := by
  rw [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  intro a
  have ha : Abundant 12 := by decide
  use (2 * (a + 1)) * 12
  grind [Abundant.mul_left ha (show 2 * (a + 1) ≠ 0 by grind)]

theorem infinite_odd_abundant : {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ n.Abundant}.Infinite := by
  rw [Set.infinite_iff_exists_gt]
  intro a
  have ha : Abundant 945 := by decide +kernel
  use (2 * a + 1) * 945
  grind [Abundant.mul_left ha (show 2 * a + 1 ≠ 0 by grind)]

end Nat
